LESSON: MELODY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.7: Melody
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Melody, part of Creating and Executing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How can one create interesting melodies?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sing the solfa syllables doh to doh1 ascending and descending,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. aurally recognise sol-fa sounds doh to doh1 in familiar melodies,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. compose short melodies within the range of doh to doh1

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. write the sol-fa syllables using calligraphy lettering,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. appreciate melodies created by self and others.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Melody in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. sing the solfa syllables doh to doh1 ascending and descending,

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. perform the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs,

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. aurally recognise sol-fa sounds doh to doh1 in familiar melodies,

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. compose short melodies within the range of doh to doh1

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. write the sol-fa syllables using calligraphy lettering,

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. appreciate melodies created by self and others.

   Melody helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  sing solfa syllable doh to doh1 ascending and descending with accuracy in pitch, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.  imitate solfa pitches sung or played on a melodic instrument for pitch discrimination, Learners with speech difficulties could be provided with variety of alternative corresponding activities.  listen to and sing familiar songs within the d-d 1 range using solfa syllables,  practice singing and performing the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  sing solfa syllable doh to doh1 ascending and descending with accuracy in pitch, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications.  imitate solfa pitches sung or played on a melodic instrument for pitch discrimination, Learners with speech difficulties could be provided with variety of alternative corresponding activities.  listen to and sing familiar songs within the d-d 1 range using solfa syllables,  practice singing and performing the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Melody together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Creativity and imagination: the learner will make thoughtful choices in selecting solfa syllables and note values to combine

using various techniques to compose melodies.

 Critical thinking and Problem solving: developed when the learner listens and recognises sol-fa sounds in melodies as well

as in interpretation of hand signs.

Values:

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

 Mentorship and peer education: enhanced through appraising and correcting peers’ compositions.

 Talent identification - Learner develops musical talent by composing and singing melodies.

Link to other learning areas:

 Mathematics: Number concept and sequencing learnt in Mathematics is applied in combination of solfa syllables in

stepwise motion and leaps.

 English: Vowels learnt in English are used to sing the solfa syllables ascending and descending.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. sing the solfa syllables doh to doh1 ascending and descending,
2. perform the sol-fa ladder using Kodaly hand signs,
3. aurally recognise sol-fa sounds doh to doh1 in familiar melodies,
4. compose short melodies within the range of doh to doh1
5. write the sol-fa syllables using calligraphy lettering,
6. appreciate melodies created by self and others.

Remember the key question: How can one create interesting melodies?
